finding: the 322 Hz acceptance criterion has no domain at 50 cm: closing the loop LOWERS the level at that frequency, so "what the loop adds" is negative and the rule cannot show anything

runs_at_50cm.note: levelling loop aborted on a clipped step (code defect, fixed)

mechanism: No saturation on any arm, so the lower bypass level is not clamping or limiting.
Closing the loop reduces the 322 Hz level by 1.67 dB, i.e. g*H is close to anti-phase there: at this frequency the loop acts as negative feedback.
The cancel arm restores the level to about the open value (-20.19 against -20.25), which is what a working canceller does to a loop - it removes the loop effect, not a benefit.

The acceptance rule presumes the loop ADDS level at the test frequency ("what the loop adds and a canceller can at most recover"). At 50 cm that premise is false, so a PASS or FAIL there carries no meaning about cancellation.
not_claimed: this does NOT show that cancellation fails at 50 cm. The operator reports good broadband amplification at 50-60 cm; a single-frequency anti-phase point does not contradict that.

options.A: choose test frequencies where g*H is in phase at each distance (scan the band, pick where the loop boost is positive) - changes the acceptance frequency, needs captain/B approval
options.B: define a broadband A/B criterion with strictly identical speech content and geometry - bigger change, needs a new protocol
options.C: keep the verified 115 cm result for this round and state 50 cm as unverifiable with the current criterion
